title: Infinite sums and products: König’s theorem and restrictions on powers

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 45–47 (§10, Theorem 10.12 and Corollary 10.13; §11, Definition 11.1 and Theorem 11.6)

summary: König’s inequality links indexed sums and products and limits the possible sizes of power sets.
abstract: Countably many one-element sets have a countable disjoint union, whereas the ways to choose from countably many two-element sets are uncountable. König’s theorem makes this comparison general: if every set in one indexed family is smaller than its partner in another, the disjoint union of the smaller sets is smaller than the set of all choices from the larger ones. Assuming the axiom of choice, this gives restrictions on infinite powers that ordinary multiplication does not reveal. In particular, the cardinality of the real numbers cannot be the limit of a countable increasing sequence of smaller cardinals.
